chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated, he said: Ibn Jabalah narrated to us from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the woman who comes performing Hajj al-Tamattu', and she experiences menstruation before she performs Tawaf al-Ifadah (the circumambulation for Tamattu') until she goes out to 'Arafat. He said: 'She becomes a single Hajj.' I said: 'Is there something upon her?' He said: 'Blood that she sheds, and it is her sacrificial offering.'
His saying (peace be upon him) 'upon her is blood that she sheds' is according to preference (istihbab), not obligation (wajib). And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.تَطُوفُ بِالْبَيْتِ: She circumambulates the Kaaba (specifically Tawaf al-Ifadah)
key_terms.حَجَّةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: Single Hajj (referring to the validity of the current pilgrimage without needing to repeat it)
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: 'Arafat (the plain where the standing of Hajj takes place)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who menstruates before Tawaf al-Ifadah during Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' who menstruates before Tawaf al-Ifadah retains the validity of her Hajj as a single pilgrimage, avoiding the need to repeat it. The required compensation is the shedding of blood (sacrificing an animal), which the text notes is recommended (*mustahabb*) rather than strictly obligatory, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the flexibility of compensatory rites for women during the sacred months.
